description:
MATERIAL. Every token is built from one primitive only: the axis-aligned or slightly rotated SQUARE, drawn with partial alpha so squares stain each other where they overlap. There are no curves, no lines, no strokes, no text — just filled quads of varying size on a near-black ground. Sizes run from large (a fifth of the frame) down to a few pixels, and the small ones read as grain.

WHAT IT IS A PICTURE OF. Each token is a radial rosette, a mandala, centred exactly in the frame. Rotational symmetry of order six to eight (1243682 and 1283437 read six-lobed; 1203347 reads seven or eight; 1310661 reads as a ring rather than a star). The structure is consistently two-zoned: a bright cream/ivory CORE at the centre, near-solid, often with a lobed or petalled silhouette, and around it a SURROUND of large discrete ochre, brown, grey and white squares arranged in one or two orbital bands, which then thins outward into a scatter of small squares that runs off the edges of the frame. The reading is somewhere between a snowflake, a rose window, and a bloom — a bright object with debris in orbit around it. Some cores carry a square-in-square recursive texture (1283437, 1243682, 1733538, 1985692, and clearly in holdout-single-512), which is the only hint of a subdivision process rather than pure placement.

PALETTE. One palette family across all twelve, no exceptions: black ground, ivory/cream, ochre-mustard-amber, dark chocolate brown, and a cool grey ramp from near-white to charcoal. Warm metal and bone against black. Nothing is saturated, nothing is a primary. Contrast is carried mostly by value (cream against black) with ochre as the single chromatic accent and grey as the connective tissue.

WHAT THE TWELVE SHARE. Black ground, dead-centre radial symmetry, squares-only vocabulary, bright core against darker surround, the same palette, and outward decay into edge scatter. There is no doubt they are one project.

HOW THEY DIFFER. Mostly by CORE SIZE, DENSITY, and HUE DOMINANCE. 1203347 is a huge pale mass that nearly fills the frame with only a thin surround left. 1985692 is a big bloom where ochre dominates the core itself rather than the surround — the only token where the warm colour is inside. 1991107 is a wide cream flower with a dark, granular, almost rotten centre. Against those, 1561509 is tiny: a small pale star in a mostly empty black field with sparse dust. 1446330 is the outlier for colour — near-monochrome grey and black, almost no ochre, with a dark hollow centre and loose scattered squares; it reads coldest and emptiest. 1310661 is the other outlier for form: a fat black ANNULUS separating the pale core from the outer band, so it reads as an eclipse or an iris rather than a flower. 1366079 is the busiest, edge-to-edge overlap with a muddled tan centre. 1475115 and 1835793 are the two closest to each other and to 1203347 — a broad pale polygon with a grey and ochre surround.

THE THREE STATES (seen on 1203347, 1243682, 1283437, 1310661). The direction of travel is consistent across all four seeds and I could state it without labels. NEUTRAL is the crispest: petals are separated, the core silhouette is articulated and star-like, internal texture is visible. STRESS SWELLS AND SOFTENS: the core inflates, its lobes fill in toward a rounder and smoother mass, internal texture is bleached out, and the surround is pushed outward — 1203347 stress is nearly a featureless white blob, 1243682 and 1283437 both fatten from a sharp star to a full flower, 1310661's core grows and its black ring thins into a smoother grey band. RECOVERY RE-ARTICULATES AND ADDS GRIT: the core contracts back toward its neutral silhouette and, decisively, a rim of small bright WHITE SQUARE GRANULES appears around the core's perimeter — obvious on 1283437 recovery and 1310661 recovery, where the granules sit like frost or gravel on the inner edge of the ring — and often a dark speck or dark centre opens up (1243682 recovery gains a distinct black dot at centre; 1203347 recovery regains petal separation and gains light specks). So: stress = swollen, smoothed, bleached, loss of structure; recovery = contracted, re-crystallised, speckled with white grain, dark centre. It is a legible three-step story, not a colour swap.

WHAT SURVIVES AT 120px. Silhouette, density, and hue dominance all survive; internal texture does not. At 120 the twelve still read as twelve: the big pale mass (1203347), the eclipse ring (1310661), the grey emptiness (1446330), the tiny star in a void (1561509), the ochre bloom (1985692), the dark-centred flower (1991107) are each identifiable across the room. The recursive square-in-square texture inside the petals is gone by 120 — it becomes a slight warm mottling — so 1283437 and 1243682 lose some of what makes them distinct at 256, and 1203347 / 1475115 / 1835793 converge into a similar 'pale polygon in a ring of squares' silhouette. The state rows also survive at 120, though unevenly: 1310661 and 1283437 recovery are unmistakable because the white granule rim is a value event, whereas 1203347's three states at 120 differ mostly in the SIZE and edge-softness of one white mass, which is the weakest of the four.

ARTIFACTS. Squares are cut by the frame on all four edges of essentially every token; in the dense tokens (1985692, 1366079, 1203347) this reads as deliberate bleed, but in the sparse ones a single lone ochre or grey square hanging half-off a corner (1243682 top-left, 1561509's corner dots, the left edge of nearly every tile) reads more like leftover than intent. Alpha stacking muddies where many squares pile up: the centre of 1366079 is an indistinct tan smear, and 1203347 under stress loses all internal information to a flat white field. Nothing is broken, nothing is empty, and I see no vanished strokes or collisions that read as bugs.
